LanguageData.CC_Settings_GoodsComeAndGo: Goods and people come and go on the map
LanguageData.CC_Settings_GoodsComeAndGo_Tip:
When an event gives the colony silver, goods, a gift or a payment owed, or takes goods it gave, sold or paid, people come to do it on the map. A few hours later, by day, a runner, a few porters or couriers from a people at peace with the colony walk in from the edge of the map: the event's own people when they can, else the neighbors whose town is nearest. They set down what they bring by the colony's gate, or walk to the stores and carry off what they came for, or wait at the gate while one of your colonists carries it out to them. A big load comes with a pack animal from their own caravans. They stay a little and walk off.

They only come when it's safe, and leave at the first sign of danger. If they can't come, can't reach the stores or can't finish, what's left of the deal is settled the old way: things owed to the colony are left where traders leave their goods, and goods owed by it leave the stores. Hurt or arrest one of them and the deal holds only as far as it got.

The people a world event's letter speaks of come too: the rider or the family waits at the gate while you answer (and a family you take in is the one that joins), guests given a night stay it and go at first light, and herds, mourners and passing bands cross the land. They come only from a people at peace with the colony and only when it's safe, and go if they're hurt, if raiders come or if the weather gets to them.

Off: everything is handed over at once, and the letters tell the rest, as before.
